classic.description: The current rules and familiar role mix, scaling with your village.
classic.illusions_description: Phantasm, Counterfeiter and Exorcist join the cast. Oathkeeper arrives at 8 players.
classic.original_description: Oracle and Veilweaver lead the village. Larger gatherings add Warden, Lamplighter, Medium, Dreamweaver and Bellkeeper.
hard.eyebrow: Follow the evidence. Doubt the evidence.
hard.description: For 5+ players. Tracker follows someone’s night target; Counterfeiter can forge an Oracle reading.
hard.details: At 7: Exorcist and Phantasm. At 8: Herbalist protects the village once. At 9: Dreamweaver. At 10: Oathkeeper. Oracle and Veilweaver remain.
chaos.eyebrow: The tide writes its own rules
chaos.description: For 5+ players. Random roles, possible duplicates, and the usual Town/Cult split. The cast is drawn when the match starts.
chaos.maelstrom_description: Each night announces a new rule: reversed Oracle readings, village-wide curse protection, or invisible visits. Everyone sees which rule is in effect.
chaos.wildcards_description: Any role can appear. Multiple Oracles, rival forgeries, a chorus of bells: nobody knows what the village will draw.
paranoia.description: For 5+ players. Any role can appear, including duplicates. The Town/Cult split is known, but the dealt role counts stay secret until the match ends. No role is guaranteed.
paranoia.oaths: Everyone can publicly promise a vote. Only an Oathkeeper who keeps that promise earns protection from new curses. Making an oath never proves your role.
paranoia.timers: Discussion gets shorter at one-third and two-thirds ritual progress. Each dawn announces your time to talk; voting time stays the same.
custom.description: Enable roles, then choose how many. Every newly enabled role starts at 1. Your exact cast must match the players at the table when you start.
custom.invalid_count: Enter a whole count from 1 to {maxPlayers} for {value}.
custom.ready: Ready for {total} players. No extra roles will be added. You can invite everyone after creating the room.
